newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican TV chief urges clemency for death row man.
newsitem.headline: Vatican TV chief urges clemency for death row man.

text.p: The Vatican's televison station on Monday made an impassioned plea for clemency for U.S. death-row prisoner Joseph O'Dell, who is due to be executed by lethal injection this week.

"I supplicate you to concede Joseph O'Dell to cross the Sacred Gates of the year 2000 and not those of death," Monsignor Guido Todeschini, director of the Roman Catholic network Telepace, wrote in a letter to the governor of Virginia, George Allen.

Pope John Paul and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi have led a chorus of protest against O'Dell's sentence. Italy, which has no death penalty in civilian criminal cases, is among the biggest supporters of a worldwide ban on capital punishment.

Prodi told Italian reporters in Luxembourg on Monday that he had made a "last, very strong, heartfelt appeal" to Allen. "We have to show that for Italy, the death penalty is something that cannot coexist with our sense of ethics," he added.
Appeals for clemency led by Italy helped win O'Dell, whose case had received little attention within the United States, a stay of execution last year.
But last month the Supreme Court upheld a death sentence passed in 1986 for the rape and murder of 44-year-old secretary Helen Schartner. O'Dell is due to die on Wednesday.

Telepace, which can be seen across the United States, said in a statement that Todeschini's appeal, in English, would be read on air at 7.30 p.m. (1730 GMT) on Monday. The station broadcasts to three continents by digital satellite from its base in Rome.
Anti-death penalty group Hands Off Cain has called a vigil outside the U.S. embassy in Rome at 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) on Monday.
It also plans a rally on Wednesday at which it intends to hold up cards with the names of 3,150 U.S. death-row prisoners.
O'Dell says he is innocent and his supporters say DNA tests prove he did not carry out the crime.
"I'm asking you to grant Joseph O'Dell the possibility of proving the fact he is supporting and against which he's been condemned," Todeschini said.
Leoluca Orlando, the mayor of the Sicilian capital Palermo where O'Dell has asked to be buried, flew to the United States on Monday to appeal to Allen on O'Dell's behalf.
Protesters in Palermo, which has granted O'Dell honorary citizenship, on Sunday staged a rally against his execution.
